extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for primary/common-school teachers on managing pupil discipline, exercising moral authority, and conducting religious influence within a school setting. Covers private admonition, cultivation of personal influence, limits of official religious/political expression, and suggested routines for religious exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private frank dealing with a delinquent pupil
rubrics_metrics.description: Go directly and frankly to the individual pupil, privately discussing the fault rather than addressing it publicly in school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask permission to speak, invite honest and open responses, describe the pupil's conduct mildly (no harsh epithets), acknowledge palliating considerations (e.g., thoughtlessness), state the teacher's duty and the necessity of change, and ask the pupil to state what he will do. Example: the teacher walked home with James, obtained his consent to speak, narrated the fault gently, and elicited an honest promise to reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate acquaintance to gain personal ascendancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately cultivate acquaintance with pupils, notice and show appreciation for their good character and conduct, and occasionally request their assistance to gain personal influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small kindnesses and opportunities for cooperation so the teacher becomes a personal influence; this increases the effectiveness of later private admonitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and deliberateness of admonition
rubrics_metrics.description: Private admonitions are generally better after a little delay and should be deliberate rather than impulsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay allows the teacher to gather circumstances and approach tenderly and cautiously. Yet when acted, the teacher must be decided and unbending as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: indulgent in judgment but firm in purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing misconduct, the teacher's attitude toward the pupil's guilt should be indulgent and palliating, while the teacher's determination to secure reform must be firm and decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine gentleness about the person's motives with clear resolve to prevent continuance and spread of the practice; balance tenderness with authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, frank, and honest dealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversations with pupils must be open and frank—no insinuations, hints, or surmises; require mutual honesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The teacher should model honesty by fully stating his observations and expectations, and require the pupil to answer honestly before determining further measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of written communication when delicate
rubrics_metrics.description: In many cases communication of reproof or moral counsel may be made most delicately and successfully in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written admonition can touch feelings more delicately than public exposure; avoid dragging private feelings before the school as punishment since that may harden or stupefy moral sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid public exposure and harsh reproaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publicly expose or vociferously reproach pupils in ways that destroy sensitiveness of conscience or harden feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harsh public exposures can lead to pupils being insensitive to reproof; delicacy preserves moral feeling and makes private reproofs effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal influence first; more vigorous measures only if necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ moral influence and the course outlined (cultivation, private admonition) first; if these fail, resort to more vigorous and decided measures determined by circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The teacher should do all moral influence will carry him; where it fails, other restraints or punishments may be required and must be firm and unbending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher's constitutional stance: authority, not persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout governance maintain the tone and manner of authority (a 'monarchy'), not of mere persuasion, while remaining morally principled and forbearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let it be seen that the teacher's constitution of the school is an absolute monarchy in structure, but that the ruler is guided by moral principle; exhibit an 'eagle eye' and 'efficient hand' for arresting evils even while proceeding gently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use official station to promote unrelated opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher has no right, by virtue of official ascendency, to use his position to promote political, religious, or other opinions foreign to the specific purposes for which he is employed, unless by express or implied consent of employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between influence as a private citizen and the strong ascendency of official station. Avoid interfering between parent and child on matters outside the teacher's trust; only act beyond specific duties with the consent of those who employ you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constrain religious instruction to common ground of patrons
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious and moral instruction in school must be confined to those principles commonly accepted by the teacher's employers (parents/founders) — the 'common ground'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what serious, thinking members of the local community commonly accept; confine moral and religious teaching to those points so as not to alienate patrons. If founders forbid religious instruction, submit or seek other employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core religious principles generally safe to teach
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a broad set of religious beliefs commonly accepted (e.g., belief in God; responsibility to God; immortality of the soul; revelation/Bible; duty of personal attachment to God; need of penitence and forgiveness through a Saviour) that a teacher may, in ordinary cases, assume and teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these common principles as the limits of acceptable religious influence in many communities, while avoiding sectarian controversies or denominational specifics unless supported by patrons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sectarian or denominational proselytizing without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not promote forms, practices, or doctrinal peculiarities of any denomination in a mixed community unless the patrons are united and consent (express or tacit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In denominationally founded schools a teacher may enforce denominational views; in mixed districts (e.g., Quakers, Roman Catholics vs Protestants) avoid forms or doctrines that would contradict parents' wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and adaptation in religious exhortation
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious exhortation must be sincere and adapted to the mental habits and character of the pupils; do not use religion merely as leverage for authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children detect hypocrisy; avoid formal, cant, or pulpit-like exhortation. Only address personal piety (penitence, trust, love for the Saviour) when the teacher's own heart is warmed and the method fits the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended structure for school religious exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggested arrangement: morning short, specific prayer (sitting, heads on desks); a verse or two of a hymn if pupils can sing; no other regular exercises until afternoon; at close of afternoon devote ~5 minutes to brief religious instruction using varied methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prayers should be minute, particular, and school-focused; singing helps adoption; afternoon instruction should vary (explain a truth, comment on scripture, tell an anecdote), avoid formal sermon style, and be suited to pupils' interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make religious instruction interesting and varied
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach moral and religious truths in ways that interest as well as instruct; vary methods and watch pupils' reactions to ensure engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anecdotes, short scriptural passages, illustrative facts, and adapt language to children's minds. If pupils show no interest, revise method; cold or constrained exhortations have little effective tendency to do good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Store and utilize illustrative material for moral teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate a habit of noticing moral and religious aspects in readings and life so you can draw on narratives, facts, and personal observations for instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reading or travelling, treasure up occurrences and narratives that can be turned to good account in moral instruction; having material helps make lessons concrete and engaging.
